missingInputs: Live application rows and actor identity
API exposure and real request context
limits: This is a hand-authored design fixture using repository evidence, not generated output from a live snapshot.
Only document read/edit patterns are modeled. Create, delete and share actions have no inferred permissions here.
Client SQL privileges, SELECT eligibility, permitted update columns and resulting-row checks are assumed satisfied within the symbolic scenarios.

claims.statement: The application has users, organizations, projects, documents, memberships and document shares.
Projects belong to organizations and documents belong to projects; membership and share records connect users to their scopes.
Reading requires authentication and live organization membership, then an administrative/editor path, a direct share, or published/archived content in a readable project.
Editing requires authentication, live organization membership, a non-archived old document and an admin, project-editor or editor-share path.
A direct editor share permits a live organization member to edit non-archived documents, but cannot override archived state.
Document updates are column-restricted and require editable old rows and readable resulting rows.

Symbolic scenarios hold the client execution path, SQL privilege checks, SELECT eligibility, permitted columns and resulting-row validation satisfied. They are not live permissions for a named person.
Organization, project, role, share and document lifecycle concepts can provide navigation lenses.
The metadata snapshot does not supply users, membership rows, share rows, request context or independent intended behavior.
